title: [C17T3] Average Weekly Spending by families
prompt: The chart below gives information about how families in one country spent their weekly income in 1968 and in 2018. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar chart compares the proportion of weekly family expenditure across eight different categories between 1968 and 2018.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, while spending on leisure activities, transport and housing saw considerable increases over the 50-year period, the percentages for most other categories, particularly food, declined significantly. Additionally, leisure became the highest spending category in 2018.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at the categories that experienced growth, leisure activities, transport and housing accounted for similar proportions of weekly spending in 1968, ranging from 7% to 10%. By 2018, leisure activities had seen the most substantial rise to 22%, becoming the highest expenditure category. Housing costs also doubled to 20%, while transport spending increased more moderately to 12%.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding the remaining categories, food clearly dominated household expenditure in 1968 at 35%, while personal goods, clothing and footwear, and fuel and power each made up around 8-10% of weekly spending. However, by 2018, food costs had fallen dramatically to just 15%, and the other three categories had also declined to between 3-4% each. Meanwhile, spending on household goods, which stood at 7% in 1968, showed little change over the 50-year period.
